subject: Encryption controls & residency: post-demo recap and decision framework
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@finbridge.com>, Priya Rao <priya.rao@lexpay.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Oct 2027 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Encryption controls & residency: post-demo recap and decision framework

Sam / Priya — thanks again for taking the demo this morning. Quick recap and proposed decision framework so we can align on next steps and what your security team will need to validate:  

1) Scope of PII + retention: you mentioned account numbers, transaction metadata, and free-text support chats. Please confirm whether chat transcripts should be treated as PII for storage/retention purposes (FinBridge policy or regulatory requirement).

2) Encryption requirements: in-transit TLS is standard; the three items to resolve are:  
  - At-rest: AES-256 encryption for data at rest (default) vs customer-managed keys (BYOK).
  - Key control: Do you require keys stored in your cloud KMS (AWS KMS / GCP KMS / Azure Key Vault) or an HSM-backed tenant?
  - Dual custody/HSM: any requirement for FIPS 140-2/3 HSM attestation or separate key escrow?

3) Logging & audit: you asked for immutable audit logs for key access and inference requests (retention window, tamper evidence). We'll surface request-level traces and token-level cost breakdowns — need to know retention duration and whether logs are allowed to leave the EU/US.

4) Residency: you flagged a preference for US-only processing for cardholder data; confirm whether routing must be region-locked or if geo-fallback is acceptable for DR.

Attached are two artifacts: a short one-pager on our KMS/BYOK options and a spreadsheet template for your data classification that helps Security sign off faster.

Proposed next steps:
- Sam: confirm which datasets are PII (simple yes/no per row in the attached spreadsheet) by EOD Tue (10/5).
- FinBridge security: confirm whether BYOK is mandatory or optional for the pilot. If BYOK, specify provider + key rotation policy.
- Redwood: internal alignment with security (Marissa), and provide an HSM/attestation checklist and estimated time to configure BYOK for a dedicated pilot (Ben).

I copied Marissa (security lead for pilots) and Ben (technical program lead) to own follow-ups. Happy to set a focused call with your security team next week.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[jonas@redwood.com] | +1 415-555-0199

[Attachment: redwood-kms-options-onepager.pdf (pdf, 215 KB)]
[Attachment: finbridge-data-classification.xlsx (xlsx, 48 KB)]

From: Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@finbridge.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@lexpay.io>
Date: Fri, 2 Oct 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Encryption controls & residency: post-demo recap and decision framework

Thanks Jonas — very helpful summary. A few clarifications from our side:  

- PII scope: we'll mark chat transcripts as sensitive if they contain cardholder data or government IDs; for other free-text we may apply tokenization. I'll populate the spreadsheet.
- BYOK: For production we mandate BYOK in our KMS (AWS KMS) for key custody. For the pilot, we can evaluate Redwood-managed keys initially if you provide strong audit capabilities and an easy migration path to BYOK.
- HSM / attestation: we need a letter confirming FIPS 140-2 HSM for keys in the provider-managed path OR an HSM-backed BYOK option. Can you provide the exact language/security artifacts we can pass to procurement?
- Logs retention: Procurement prefers 7 years for audit logs related to payments; Security may push back on that for volume reasons — what's the compression/archival options? Also, can logs be anchored (hashes) into an immutability ledger?

Also — what is your expected SLA impact (latency/cost) when using BYOK vs Redwood-managed keys with your default caching/batching? That will help our performance team decide.

If you can share the HSM attestation checklist and a short paragraph we can drop into our SOC/Procurement package, that'd accelerate things.

Sam
Head of Platform Security | FinBridge
sam.jenkins@finbridge.com | +1 212-555-4466

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@finbridge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 3 Oct 2027 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Encryption controls & residency: post-demo recap and decision framework

Sam — thanks, noted. Quick replies inline and actions below:  

- PII scope: great — once you flag rows in the spreadsheet we'll produce a scoping statement that maps each dataset to storage/retention policy (retention TTLs, masking/tokenization where needed).

- BYOK: we support both modes: (A) Redwood-managed keys (AES-256 at rest) with dedicated audit streams; (B) Customer BYOK via AWS KMS (we also support GCP/Azure). For BYOK we provide rotation orchestration but the key material lifecycle remains in your KMS. We also have an HSM-backed option for Private deployments where keys can be kept in an HSM in your VPC.

- HSM attestation artifacts: attaching a short checklist and standard attestation paragraph you can paste into procurement materials. It includes our FIPS/HSM claims, supported providers, and what evidence we can provide for a pilot.

- Logs retention & immutability: audit logs are exportable to your storage (S3/GCS) with configurable retention and can be hashed into an append-only ledger on demand. For very long retention (7+ years) we recommend an archival pipeline to your bucket (compressed) — Ben, see item below on sizing/cost estimate.

- SLA impact: preliminary guidance — BYOK in AWS KMS introduces modest additional latency on key unwrap for initial tokenization operations; once keys are cached in-memory at our serving runtime the per-request delta is minimal. I'll have Ben quantify expected 95th percentile token latency and incremental cost by Monday.

Action items (owners):
- Sam / FinBridge: mark PII rows in attached spreadsheet (due Tue 10/5) — Sam
- Redwood (Marissa): send HSM attestation + short procurement paragraph (attached) — Marissa
- Redwood (Ben): provide pilot-level time estimate to wire BYOK in a dedicated pilot and a brief note on expected latency/cost delta — Ben

Attaching: "redwood-hsm-attestation-checklist.pdf" (one-page) for your procurement packet.

Happy to get on a 30-min security deep-dive with your security and performance teams next Wed or Thu — let me know availability.

Best,
Jonas
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

[Attachment: redwood-hsm-attestation-checklist.pdf (pdf, 64 KB)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2027 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Encryption controls & residency: post-demo recap and decision framework

Thanks team — I prepared the HSM attestation paragraph and the short checklist Jonas referenced. Dropping the procurement-ready language below so Sam/FinBridge can copy it into their docs.

--- Begin attestation text ---
Redwood Inference provides optional HSM-backed key custody for Private and Dedicated deployments. For BYOK deployments using customer KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault), Redwood performs key usage via KMS API calls; the key material remains under customer control. For provider-managed keys, we persist data encrypted with AES-256 at rest; key rotation and key-wrapping are handled by Redwood with segregation of duties and monthly rotation by default.

Evidence available for pilot: FIPS 140-2/3 certificate (for HSM vendors), configuration checklist, and logs demonstrating KMS API calls and key usage timestamps. For procurement, we can provide a signed statement and sample configuration snippets for AWS KMS (alias usage, IAM roles) plus an Attestation Checklist PDF.
--- End attestation text ---

Ben — can you attach the sizing/cost delta for the pilot (BYOK in AWS KMS vs Redwood-managed keys) and a 1-paragraph note on latency at 95th percentile so we have a single doc to drop into the HubSpot deal? I'll assemble everything and upload to the Drive link Jonas shared.

Marissa Cole
